Ollama · LM Studio · llama.cpp · Boole

Ollama vs LM Studio vs llama.cpp vs Boole.

Four different ways to run a model on your own machine. This page compares what each project documents. It does not rank them by speed.

No invented benchmarks. Boole has not measured Ollama, LM Studio, or llama.cpp against the Boole CLI. The only speed we publish is 12.3 tok/s for the in-browser SmolLM2 135M demo, on a 4-core Xeon, WebAssembly, one thread, no GPU layers. A 20B model at 200 tok/s is a goal.

The four tools

CLI and local server

Ollama

A local runner with ollama run, ollama pull, and ollama serve. The project is MIT-licensed. Its FAQ says a local server binds 127.0.0.1 port 11434, and that prompts from a local run are not sent to ollama.com. Cloud-hosted models are a separate path in that same FAQ.

Desktop app

LM Studio

A desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Its docs say it runs GGUF models through llama.cpp, and MLX on Apple Silicon. A local server starts from the Developer tab or lms server start. The OpenAI-compatible examples use port 1234. The app terms treat the source as the company’s, and license it for personal and internal business use.

The engine

llama.cpp

The C/C++ project behind a lot of local GGUF inference. MIT-licensed. Current docs at llama.app show llama cli for the terminal and llama serve for an OpenAI-compatible API and web UI on 127.0.0.1 port 9931. The README lists Metal, CUDA, Vulkan, and other backends.

Managed, or a small CLI

Boole

Boole AI, Inc. sells a managed setup for $1,800 and, separately, a codebase inquiry. @boole/cli 0.7.0 needs Node.js 22 or newer. Commands: run, pull, doctor, models, list, and serve. serve is local development only, with no authentication, and it accepts POST /generate.

What each one documents

OllamaMIT license (LICENSE). Local server at 127.0.0.1:11434 (FAQ). OpenAI-compatible subset at /v1 on that port (docs). Default context in the FAQ is 4096 tokens. Local runs stay local; the FAQ describes a different path for cloud models.
LM StudioDesktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux (docs). llama.cpp for GGUF, plus MLX on Apple Silicon. Server via the Developer tab or lms server start (server). Examples use http://localhost:1234/v1 (OpenAI compatibility). App terms (23 Aug 2026) license personal and internal business use and restrict redistribution and service-bureau use. Source is not offered as an open-source grant.
llama.cppMIT-licensed C/C++ (repository). GGUF. Introduction: llama cli and llama serve. Server docs: default listen address 127.0.0.1:9931, OpenAI-compatible /v1 routes, Metal and CUDA among the backends in the README. You build or install it yourself.
BooleProprietary CLI from Boole AI, Inc., @boole/cli 0.7.0, on Node.js 22 or newer. First: npx @boole/cli doctor (--json optional). Then pull and run a model, for example bartowski/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M. list prints downloaded models. serve is local development only, no authentication, POST /generate. Managed entry payment $1,800. Codebase acquisition is an inquiry to hello@booleinference.com.

When to use which

Use Ollama when you want a local runner that already has a documented server and an OpenAI-compatible subset, and you are comfortable operating it.

Use LM Studio when you want a desktop app, a chat window, and a local server without building llama.cpp. Read their terms before you redistribute anything or offer it as a service.

Use llama.cpp when you want the engine itself: the binary, the server, and the backends upstream ships. Boole does not claim to be a faster build of it.

Use Boole’s managed tier when you want Boole AI, Inc. to set the local system up and run it. Use the Boole CLI, and the device guides, when you want to run it yourself. serve is a local development server, not a hosted API.

Questions

Which one is fastest?

Boole has not published a speed comparison against Ollama, LM Studio, or llama.cpp. The only measured number on this site is the browser demo: 12.3 tok/s for SmolLM2-135M Instruct Q4_K_M, 64 tokens, about 5187 ms, on a 4-core Xeon CPU in WebAssembly, one thread, no GPU layers. A 20B model at 200 tok/s is a goal, not a measurement.

Is the Boole CLI a drop-in replacement for Ollama?

No. Ollama’s docs describe a local server on 127.0.0.1 port 11434 and an OpenAI-compatible subset at /v1. @boole/cli 0.7.0 has run, pull, doctor (--json), models, list, and serve. serve is for local development only, has no authentication, and accepts POST /generate. That is not Ollama’s /v1 API. It needs Node.js 22 or newer.

What is Boole actually built on?

The CLI imports node-llama-cpp 3.22.2, which runs llama.cpp and GGUF files. It is a thin command line on that runtime, plus a separate WebAssembly demo. It is not a fork we claim is faster than upstream.
